tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

Resolve only from tenant-scoped published owner-map aliases whose historical identifier matches and whose inclusive effective interval covers the source event timestamp. Evaluate all qualifying records: resolve only if they all identify the same canonical published service; if they identify multiple canonical services, keep signals separate and render ownership as explicit unknown, independent of storage order. Requested changes on **lantern#3037**. The PR picks the first matching alias, making overlapping records storage-order dependent, and falls back to name similarity. The established rule requires evaluating all tenant-scoped aliases whose inclusive intervals cover the event timestamp: resolve only when they agree on one canonical service; otherwise keep signals separate and show ownership as explicit unknown. No qualifying alias also means unknown—never infer from similar names. The review is submitted; the PR remains open.

pr.title: Resolve historical owner-map aliases

changed_files.summary: The resolver iterates owner-map alias rows in storage order. For rows matching the tenant and historical identifier, it returns the first row whose effective_start <= source_event_timestamp <= effective_end, using that row's canonical_service_id. If no interval match is found, it selects a canonical service in the same tenant using normalized service-name similarity.

pr.diff_summary: Overlapping active aliases are resolved by the first matching record in storage order. When no interval match exists, the patch infers a rename from similar service names.

args.body: This does not match the established service-identity rule. Resolve only from tenant-scoped published owner-map aliases whose historical identifier matches and whose inclusive effective interval covers the source event timestamp. Evaluate all qualifying records: resolve only if they all identify the same canonical published service; if they identify multiple canonical services, keep signals separate and render ownership as explicit unknown, independent of storage order. If no alias qualifies (including timestamps outside the interval), keep signals separate with explicit unknown ownership. Remove normalized-name similarity fallback entirely; Lantern must not infer identity from similar names or context. Please add regressions for overlapping aliases in both row orders, both inclusive endpoints, a single valid match, no matching alias, and ambiguous/no-cover cases.
